The brand in six rules.

Dark story sections, cream sections where people compare, one orange. Everything below follows from these.

  1. 01

    Write to "you"About the person in motion, never about boxes.

  2. 02

    Two-weight headlinesUppercase. Light for the setup, Heavy for the payoff.

  3. 03

    Orange is an accentBars, icons and the one primary action of a view. Sections stay neutral.

  4. 04

    One squared cornerCards are 0 R R R. Controls are full pills. Checkboxes and radios are circles.

  5. 05

    Show the grid2px rules edge to edge, a 5px orange bar beside each section heading.

  6. 06

    One curveease-out on transform and opacity only. All of it off under reduced motion.

Colour tokens.

Near-black grounds, warm cream and two oranges: brand for the bright marks, brand-2 for bars, focus and links on light.

Shadows and depth.

Dark sections stay flat. On light pages cards carry long, soft, warm shadows. Click one to copy its CSS.

Slow to arrive, quick to respond.

Lines rise, cards settle, a door rolls up. One house curve does almost everything.

Easing

ease-outcubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)The house curve: reveals, hovers, lifts, panels, tabs (123 uses).
ease-navcubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)Sticky nav sliding in; social-icon fill.
ease-standardcubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1)Accordion height, image cross-fades, sheen loops.
ease-doorcubic-bezier(.3,0,.55,1)Elements that rise together with the intro roll-up door.
ease-introcubic-bezier(.65,0,.15,1)The intro door itself (1.6s).
ease-pingcubic-bezier(0,0,.2,1)Pulsing 'live' dots.
ease-shakecubic-bezier(.36,.07,.19,.97)Error shake on an invalid search (0.4s).

Durations

dur-fast.2sColour, border and background changes on hover and focus.
dur-base.3sFades, icon colour, tab colour.
dur-move.45sHover lifts, arrow nudges, accordion open, sticky nav.
dur-reveal.6sLine-by-line heading reveal (per line, staggered).
dur-enter1.1sHero panels rising in; rules drawing across.
dur-photo1.2sPhoto zoom inside a card on hover (scale 1.05).
dur-seal24sOne turn of the round seal's text ring (40s for the home stamp), linear.

Actions 3

Button

The pill CTA with a dark round arrow badge on the right; the only button shape Journey uses.

Loading…
variant"primary" | "outline" | "dark"primary = brand-gradient fill with a sheen on hover; outline = 1.7px border that fills dark on hover; dark = small ink-2 secondary. Default "primary".
size"lg" | "md" | "sm"lg = 63px tall, 18px label; md = 55px, 16px; sm = 48px, 14px (inside cards). Default "lg".
blockbooleanFull width with the arrow pushed to the right edge (card CTAs).
onDarkbooleanOutline variant on a dark card: cream border, label and badge.
arrowbooleanShow the arrow badge. Default true (false for "dark").
hrefstringRender an <a> instead of a <button>.
children requiredReactNode

Also accepts every native <button> attribute.

  • primary (default): brand-gradient fill with the shadow-button bevel, cream-text-2 label. On hover it lifts 2px and a white sheen sweeps across. Use once per view for the main action ("Find units", "Rent this space", "Continue").
  • outline: 1.7px outline-border on cream, ink label ("See more details"). On hover the arrow badge grows until it fills the button dark. Add onDark on dark cards: cream border, label and badge ("See sizes & prices").
  • dark: 44px ink-2 pill without arrow, for small secondary actions on light panels ("Add card", "Change").
  • size: lg (63px, button-lg) in heroes and forms; md (55px, button-md) beside inputs and in section heads; sm (48px, button-sm) inside cards, usually with block.
  • Consumer provides: the label (short verb phrase, sentence case, no trailing punctuation), href for links, and any button props (type="submit", onClick, disabled).
  • Don't drop the arrow badge on primary or outline, swap it for another icon, or stack two primaries in one view.
  • Contrast: the label on the gradient is 2.2 to 3:1, below 4.5:1 (kept exact from the site).

Hand-written from .jrny-btn in index.html and .ck-btn2 in rentaspace/checkout.html.

Arrow

The one arrow glyph of the brand: a thin line arrow with round caps, rotated by direction.

Loading…
direction"up" | "right" | "down" | "left"Direction the head points to. Default "right".
sizenumberPixel width and height. Default 20.
colorstringStroke colour. Default currentColor.
strokeWidthnumberStroke width in the 20-unit box. Default 1.65.
  • Use it inside the Button badge, round controls (39 to 42px circles), text links and carousels. It inherits currentColor.
  • Consumer provides: direction (right by default), size in px, optionally color and strokeWidth (1.65 in a 20-unit box).
  • Don't mix in chevrons or filled arrows for the same job; chevrons are only for dropdown triggers and breadcrumbs.

Hand-written from the inline SVG in .jrny-btn__ic (index.html).

TextLink

A text-only link: brand with a trailing arrow on dark cards, or underlined brand-2 inside copy on light panels.

Loading…
inlinebooleanUnderlined 14px brand-2 link for use inside copy on light panels.
arrowbooleanTrailing arrow. Default true (false when inline).
children requiredReactNode

Also accepts every native <a> attribute.

  • Default: 16px bold brand, arrow at the end; the gap to the arrow grows from 8 to 14px on hover. Use at the foot of a card or accordion row ("Compare sizes").
  • inline: 14px bold brand-2, underlined, no arrow; turns ink-2 on hover. Use inside sentences and section headers on light ("Change size", "Clear all").
  • Consumer provides: href and the label (a verb phrase or a destination, never "click here").
  • Don't use it for the main action of a view; that is a Button.

Hand-written from .jrny-rs-link (rentaspace.html) and .ck-link (rentaspace/checkout.html).

Navigation 4

NavBar

The pill-shaped primary navigation that floats over the hero, top right of the logo.

Loading…
items requiredArray<string | { label: string; href?: string; menu?: boolean }>Links in order; an object with menu: true renders a dropdown trigger with chevron.
activestringLabel of the current page (keeps the orange pill).
labelstring
classNamestring
  • 61px tall surface pill with a 1px border-dark; links are 14px Medium cream-text-2. A link under the pointer (and the current page) gets a brand pill with a 6px dot that grows in before the label.
  • Consumer provides: items (labels or {label, href}; menu: true for the "Ecosystem" dropdown trigger) and active.
  • Keep to six items or fewer. Below 900px the site replaces it with a hamburger sheet; after the hero scrolls away a sticky bar slides up from the BOTTOM of the screen (sticky, shadow-sticky).
  • The dropdown itself (a 300px radius-textarea dark sheet with icon rows) is described in the brand book, not packaged.

Hand-written from .jrny-nav .jrny-menu in index.html.

Tabs

Switches panes inside one block: an underline list inside dark panels, or a glass pill bar over photos.

Loading…
items requiredArray<{ id: string; label: ReactNode; icon?: string; count?: number }>
variant"underline" | "glass"underline = inside a dark panel; glass = blurred pill bar over a photo. Default "underline".
valuestring
defaultValuestring
onChange(id: string) => void
labelstringAccessible name of the tab list.
classNamestring
  • underline (default): 52px tabs, 14px Bold sand; the selected tab is cream-text with a 2px brand underline and a full-strength icon. An optional count shows a small brand counter (active filters).
  • glass: glass fill with glass-edge border and an 18px backdrop blur; the selected tab is a brand pill. Use only over photography (gallery categories).
  • Consumer provides: items ({id, label, icon?, count?}), value/defaultValue, onChange, and label as the accessible name. The panes are yours.
  • Keep labels to one or two words; three to four tabs.

Stepper

Checkout progress: numbered 32px circles joined by a 2px line across the full width.

Loading…
steps requiredstring[]Step labels in order.
currentnumberZero-based index of the current step; earlier steps show a check.
labelstring
classNamestring
  • Past steps are solid brand-2 with a check and a filled connector; the current step is solid with the shadow-step-on halo; future steps are white with a cream-line border and ink-soft labels.

Forms 5

TextField

A labelled pill input (or rounded textarea) in two tones: dark for contact forms, light for checkout.

Loading…
idstring
label requiredReactNodeLabel text. On dark it follows a 6px brand dot and ends with a colon ("Email:"); on light no dot, no colon.
tone"dark" | "light"dark = on surface cards; light = on white checkout panels. Default "dark".
multilinebooleanRender a 104px textarea instead of an input.
errorReactNodeError message; turns the border danger and is announced with the field.

Also accepts every native <input> attribute.

  • dark (default): input fill, 1px border-dark, 55px tall, sand text; the label is 18px Semibold cream-text after a 6px brand dot and ends with a colon ("Email:"). Focus turns the border brand-2.
  • light: paper fill, 1.5px cream-line, 54px tall, 16px text; the label is 14px Bold ink-2, no dot, no colon. Focus adds the shadow-focus halo; error turns the border danger on danger-bg and shows the message under the field.
  • Every text input is a pill (radius-full); only the textarea uses radius-textarea.
  • Consumer provides: label, id, and any input props (type, placeholder, autoComplete, required).
  • Validate when the user leaves the field; write the error as what to fix ("Enter a valid email.", "Enter a 10-digit phone number."), never "Invalid".

Hand-written from .jrny-field (index.html) and .ck-f/.ck-in (rentaspace/checkout.html).

SearchField

The hero search pill: magnifier, ZIP or city input, and a "Near me" chip that asks for the visitor's location.

Loading…
labelstringVisually hidden label. Default "Enter your ZIP or city".
nearMeboolean | stringfalse hides the geolocation chip; a string replaces its text. Default "Near me".
onNearMe() => void

Also accepts every native <input> attribute.

  • 63px tall, cream-text-2 fill with ink-2 text so it is the brightest thing on a dark hero; focus adds a brand border and a 4px orange halo.
  • Always pair it with a primary Button ("Find units") at a 20px gap; on phones they stack.
  • Consumer provides: input props (name, value, onChange), onNearMe, and label for screen readers. nearMe={false} removes the chip.
  • Placeholder is the instruction itself: "Enter your ZIP or city…".

Hand-written from .jrny-search__field in index.html.

Checkbox

A circle, never a rounded square: every checkbox and radio on the site is round.

Loading…
tone"brand" | "ink"brand = brand-2 when checked (forms, consent); ink = ink-2 when checked, with row hover (filter lists). Default "brand".
hintReactNodeSecond line under the label.
countnumberResult count shown at the right (filter lists).
errorboolean
children requiredReactNode

Also accepts every native <input> attribute.

  • brand (default): 22px circle, control-border on paper; checked is solid brand-2 with a white check. Use for consent and yes/no choices in forms.
  • ink: 20px circle that turns ink-2 when checked, inside a row that tints on hover; optional hint line and a count badge at the right. Use in filter lists.
  • Consumer provides: the label as children (a full sentence for consent), and input props (name, checked, onChange).
  • Don't square the corners, and don't use a switch for these.

Hand-written from .ck-check (rentaspace/checkout.html) and .jrny-th-check (rentaspace/templehallhwy.html).

OptionCard

A single-choice card: light when idle, and solid dark (selected) with white text once chosen.

Loading…
layout"card" | "row"card = stacked with a radio dot top-right; row = thumbnail, text, price in one line. Default "card".
title requiredReactNode
descriptionReactNode
priceReactNodePrice text, e.g. "$17".

mediastringURL of an icon (card) or a square thumbnail (row).

Also accepts every native <input> attribute.

  • card (default): stacked icon, big title (plan-amount), description and price, with a radio dot top-right; one squared corner (radius-commerce). Use for two to four parallel plans.
  • row: thumbnail, title and description, price at the right (radius-option). Use for longer lists such as unit sizes.
  • The dark selected state is the rule for every selectable card (unit, plan, saved payment card). Don't mark selection with only a coloured border.
  • Consumer provides: name and value (it is a real radio input), title, description, price, per, media, and checked/onChange.

Hand-written from .ck-plan and .ck-unit in rentaspace/checkout.html.

Voice and copy.

Journey talks to one person in the middle of something. Storage is never the subject; the change is.

Headlines

  • Storage without the friction.
  • Journeys need space.
  • Space to move on.
  • Questions? Answered.
  • Your space is waiting.

Four promises

  • Your phone is the key. "No office hours, because life doesn't keep them."
  • Open any hour, any day. "Gates open automatically. Your space is ready."
  • Clear, month-to-month pricing. "The number you see is the number you pay."
  • A real person when you need one. "When it isn't routine, someone real picks up."

Interface text

  • Buttons are sentence-case verb phrases: "Find units", "Rent this space".
  • Errors say what to do: "Enter a valid email." Never "Invalid".
  • Prices read "$29/mo", with the in-store price struck beside them.
  • Reassurance sits next to the action: "Month-to-month · no deposit".
  • No exclamation marks, emoji or hype words.
